data.q: Which package is required to use Entity Framework Core with SQL Server?
data.e: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer is the database provider package for SQL Server. The base package (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore) is a dependency but not sufficient alone.

data.q: In EF Core, which class represents a session with the database and allows you to query and save instances of your entities?
data.e: DbContext is the primary class that coordinates EF Core functionality for a given data model. It represents a session with the database.

data.q: How do you register a DbContext in the dependency injection container in an ASP.NET Core application (Program.cs)?
data.e: AddDbContext is the specific extension method for registering DbContext types. It handles scoping (default Scoped) and configuration options like the database provider.

data.q: Which method is used to apply pending migrations to the database programmatically at runtime?
data.e: Migrate() applies any pending migrations. EnsureCreated() only creates the schema if the database doesn't exist but ignores migrations.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `OnModelCreating` method in a DbContext derived class?
o: To configure the database connection string
To configure the entity model using Fluent API
data.e: OnModelCreating is overridden to configure the model (relationships, constraints, indexes, conversions) using the ModelBuilder Fluent API.

data.q: Which tracking behavior is the default for queries in EF Core?
data.e: By default, EF Core tracks query results (Tracking). Changes to tracked entities are persisted on SaveChanges(). AsNoTracking() disables this for read-only scenarios.

data.q: How do you define a one-to-many relationship using Fluent API where `Blog` has many `Posts`?
data.e: Starting from the principal (Blog), HasMany defines the collection navigation. WithOne defines the inverse reference navigation on the dependent (Post). Option D is also valid syntax starting from the dependent entity.

data.q: What does the `HasData` method in `OnModelCreating` allow you to do?
data.e: HasData is used for data seeding. EF Core manages the insertion of this data during migrations based on primary key values.

data.q: Which concurrency token strategy is commonly implemented by adding a `byte[]` property annotated with `[Timestamp]`?
data.e: A byte[] property with [Timestamp] (or IsRowVersion()) configures a Row Version column (rowversion in SQL Server) used for optimistic concurrency detection.

data.q: What is the difference between `Include()` and `ThenInclude()` in a LINQ query?
o: Include loads collections, ThenInclude loads references
Include starts eager loading, ThenInclude drills down into nested navigation properties
Include is for tracking, ThenInclude is for no-tracking
There is no difference; they are aliases
data.e: Include specifies the first navigation property to load. ThenInclude is chained after a collection Include to load related data of the collection items.

data.q: Which command creates a new migration based on model changes in the Package Manager Console (Visual Studio)?
data.e: Add-Migration scaffolds a new migration file. Update-Database applies them.

data.q: What happens if you call `SaveChanges()` and a concurrency conflict is detected (e.g., RowVersion mismatch)?
data.e: EF Core throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException. The application must catch this and resolve the conflict (e.g., reload entity, merge, or accept client values).

data.q: How do you configure a property as the Primary Key using Fluent API if it doesn't follow the 'Id' or '<Type>Id' convention?
data.e: HasKey defines the primary key for the entity type. IsPrimaryKey does not exist on PropertyBuilder.

data.q: What is the purpose of `AsSplitQuery()` (introduced in EF Core 5.0) when eager loading multiple collections?
o: Splits the query into multiple SQL queries to avoid cartesian explosion
Splits the result set into pages
Splits the entity into multiple tables (TPT)
Splits the DbContext into multiple instances
data.e: Loading multiple collections with Include in a single query creates a Cartesian product (explosion). AsSplitQuery generates separate SQL queries per collection and combines results in memory.

data.q: Which interface must a custom value converter implement to convert a property type to a database column type?
data.e: ValueConverter<TModel, TProvider> (implementing IValueConverter) defines conversion logic between the CLR type and the provider type.

data.q: In a disconnected scenario (e.g., Web API), what is the standard pattern to update an existing entity received from a client?
data.e: All three approaches attach the entity and mark it as Modified. context.Update() is the most concise modern API (EF Core 5+). Attach + State and Entry + State are lower-level equivalents.
